Chapter 01

Welcome

Welcome to the Urban Muaythai Kids Academy. Our goal isn't simply to teach children how to punch and kick. Our mission is to develop confident, respectful, resilient young people through the discipline of Muaythai.

Every child follows a structured pathway designed to build their skills, confidence and character over several years. The Academy rewards consistency, effort and positive behaviour just as much as athletic ability.

Whether your child dreams of becoming a champion or simply becoming more confident, every lesson helps them grow.

Every lesson helps them grow — whether the goal is the ring, or simply believing in themselves.

Urban Muaythai Kids Academy

Chapter 04

The Three Pillars of the Academy

Every child's progress is built on three foundations working together — technical skill, consistent attendance, and character.

01

Skill Development

Every fundamental aspect of Muaythai, built gradually through a three-year syllabus.

02

Consistency Progress

Every class earns a sticker. Consistency is tracked and celebrated on the Academy Progress Card.

03

Building Character

Attendance builds skill. Character builds champions — Stars reward who a child is becoming.

Pillar One

Skill Development

Children gradually learn every fundamental aspect of Muaythai. Each grading introduces new techniques while refining previous skills. Our grading syllabus progressively develops these skills over approximately three years.

Coordination Balance Fitness Self-Defence Confidence Discipline
  • 01Coordination
  • 02Balance
  • 03Fitness
  • 04Self-Defence
  • 05Confidence
  • 06Discipline
Pillar Two

Consistency Progress

Every child receives an Academy Progress Card. After every class they receive one attendance sticker, so parents and children can easily track progress towards their next grading.

Academy Progress Card

Each sticker marks one class attended, building visibly toward the next singlet.

Minimum Attendance Requirements

Chapter 05

Grading

Gradings are held during Week 8 of every Queensland State School Term. Students are invited once they meet all three requirements.

1

Minimum Sessions

Completed the required minimum sessions for their current singlet.

2

Technical Skill

Demonstrated the required technical skills for the next level.

3

Effort & Behaviour

Displayed consistent effort and behaviour in class.

💡

If a child hasn't reached the required number of sessions before Week 8, they'll simply continue training and be invited to the following grading. There is no disadvantage to waiting until they are ready.

Singlet 1 of 6 · White · Giraffe

Finding Your Feet

"Finding your feet begins with your first step."

Your First Step

Every new Kids Academy member begins their journey with the White Singlet. Just like a young giraffe learning to find its feet, this level is about building confidence, learning the foundations of Muay Thai, and getting comfortable on the mats.

Skills at This Level
  • Basic punches
  • Roundhouse kicks
  • Switch kicks
  • Teeps
  • Push kicks
  • Knees
  • Basic elbows
Singlet 2 of 6 · Yellow · Lion Cub

Learning When to Roar

"Learning when to Roar."

In the Grading
  • 2 x 2 min skipping
  • 2 x 2 min shadow boxing — punching, kicking, knees and footwork
  • 3 x 2 min bag work — all weapons and footwork
  • 10 min line up — set combinations to follow
  • Stretching
Instructor's Expectations
  • Correct posture during skipping
  • Knowledge & ability during shadow boxing
  • Knowledge & ability during bag rounds
  • Confidence and concentration during grading
Requirements from the White Singlet
  • Basic punches — jab, cross, hook, uppercut
  • Roundhouse kick and switch kick
  • Teep and push kick
  • Basic long knee, basic switch knee
  • Basic elbows — up, round, over
Singlet 3 of 6 · Blue · Shark

Sharpening Your Skills

"Sharpening your skills."

In the Grading
  • 3 x 2 min skipping — control rope, consistent rhythm and posture
  • 2 x 2 min shadow boxing — correct & varied techniques and footwork
  • 3 x 2 min bag work — combinations and footwork, maintain level
  • 10 min Dutch-style drills — composure, control, techniques and blocking
  • Stretching
Instructor's Expectations
  • Control of rope, rhythm and posture during skipping
  • Correct, varied techniques and footwork in shadow boxing
  • Maintains level across the 3 bag rounds
  • Confidence & composure in blocking; control in striking during Dutch drills
  • Understands how to stretch all the major body parts used
Requirements from the Yellow Singlet

Dutch style drills as a minimum:

  • 1, 2 combo followed by leg kick
  • 1, 2 combo followed by switch leg kick
  • 1, 2 combo followed by body kick
  • 1, 2 combo followed by switch body kick
  • Block punches & block left & right kicks
Singlet 4 of 6 · Green · Crocodile

Always Calm, Ready to Strike

"Always calm but ready to strike."

In the Grading
  • 3 x 2 min skipping — control rope, consistent rhythm and posture
  • 2 x 2 min shadow boxing — correct & varied techniques and footwork
  • 5 x 2 min Dutch-style drills — block and defend against attacks
  • 5 x 2 min sparring — NO HEAD CONTACT
  • Stretching
Instructor's Expectations
  • Control of rope, rhythm and posture during skipping
  • Correct, varied techniques and footwork in shadow boxing
  • Follows drills, controls technique, places attacks to the correct area
  • Composure and control in sparring, correct target area, no head contact
Requirements from the Blue Singlet

Green grading is harder — better technique, fitness/stamina and combinations for the same requirements. Dutch style drills as a minimum:

  • 1, 2 combo → leg kick and counter kick
  • 1, 2 combo → switch leg kick and counter kick
  • 1, 2 combo → body kick and counter kick
  • 1, 2 combo → switch body kick and counter kick
  • Block punches & block left & right kicks
  • Use teep as a defence while under attack
  • Use a knee as part of a combination
Singlet 5 of 6 · Purple · Eagle

Soaring High

"Soaring high, planning your next move."

In the Grading
  • 6 min skipping — control rope, consistent rhythm and posture
  • 2 x 2 min shadow boxing — correct & varied techniques and footwork
  • 5 x 2 min bag work — combinations and footwork, maintain level
  • 10 x 2 min sparring rounds — technique, defence, attack, footwork and control
  • 5 min clinching — clinch, defend, control and correct knee techniques
  • Stretching
Instructor's Expectations
  • Control of rope, rhythm and posture during skipping
  • Correct, varied techniques and footwork in shadow boxing
  • Maintains level across all 5 bag rounds
  • Composure and control for all 10 sparring rounds — pace, technique, control
  • Correct clinch technique, clinch defence and knee-strike control
Requirements from the Green Singlet

Purple grading tests stamina and grit — physical effort and determination. A lack of effort earns one warning from a head instructor; if effort must be asked for again, the grading is failed and re-attempted at the next purple singlet grading.

Singlet 6 of 6 · Black · Elephant

Strength, Durability & Longevity

"Like the Elephant in Thailand — strength, durability and longevity — the black singlet now begins a Muaythai journey."

In the Grading
  • Warm up — 10 min skipping
  • 3 x 2 min bag work — prepare for sparring, maintain level, combinations and footwork
  • 5 x 2 pad work — student of the padholder; composure, control and effort
  • 10 x 2 min sparring rounds — control emotions, attack & defence, composure under pressure
  • Speech — 3 min on what Muaythai means to them, plus a Thai greeting, counting to 10 in Thai, and thanking the trainers in Thai
Instructor's Expectations
  • Focus and effort through skipping, bag work, pad work and sparring
  • Skill and consistency in skipping — posture and focus for 10 minutes
  • Correct techniques and footwork on the bag, with great effort
  • Listens and shows correct technique and great effort on pads
  • Composure, skill, defence, attack and effort during sparring
Requirements from the Purple Singlet

This grading shows the senior instructors the student is ready to make the transition to Teacher.

  • Each sparring round is scored/judged on effort and correct technique
  • Shows attack and defensive techniques while maintaining composure under pressure
  • Prepares a 3-minute speech on the importance of Muaythai in their life, how it has changed them, and what they can offer new people

Chapter 08

Our 5 Values

At Urban Muaythai Kids Academy, our values guide how we train, how we treat each other, and how we show up every day.

🤝

Friendly & Welcoming

Everyone belongs at Urban.

Say hello, introduce yourself, welcome new people, and help others feel part of the team.

❤️

Kindness

We help and support each other.

Be a great training partner. Help during drills, encourage others, and celebrate their effort.

🙏

Respect

We respect our coaches, teammates and our gym.

Listen to your coaches, thank them, give knuckles, look after your training partners, and tidy the pads and equipment you use.

✨

Positive Mindset

We focus on what’s possible.

Challenges help us grow. Keep trying, learn from mistakes, encourage others, and believe you can improve.

⭐

Take Ownership

We give our best effort.

Take responsibility for your training, attitude and actions. Forget ‘Fine’ — aim for the stars and strive to be great.

Be Friendly. Be Kind. Show Respect. Stay Positive. Give Your Best.

Live our values. Earn your stars. Become your best.
